title: Lift and move heavy things without getting hurt
summary: Back injuries and crushed fingers end more scavenging trips than anything else. Strip the load, use levers, rollers, ramps and a second person, and never let a heavy load get ahead of you.

materials.item: Short lengths of round pipe for rollers
Wooden blocks and strong planks for packing and ramps

steps.text: Size it up. Tip one corner to feel the weight. If you can't lift a corner easily, it's a job for two people or a machine.
Make it lighter. Take off doors, drawers, panels and anything you don't need. Take the concrete weights out of a washing machine. Often the useful part is a fraction of the weight.
Plan the route: open the doors, clear the floor, check stairs, ramps and the vehicle. Decide where you'll set it down and where you can rest on the way.
Lift close and low: feet apart, one slightly forward, knees bent, back straight, a firm grip. Lift smoothly with your legs and keep the load against your body.
steps.warn: Don't twist with a load. Turn by moving your feet.

steps.text: With two people, one calls the moves: "ready, lift", "stop", "down". Go at the pace of the weaker person.
On stairs, the person below takes more weight and is in the line of a fall. Put the stronger person there, go one step at a time, and keep talking.
steps.warn: If the load starts to slide, the person below steps aside. Nobody tries to stop it with their body.

steps.text: To raise something off the floor, lever one edge up a little with a pry bar and slide a wooden block under it. Repeat, building up a stack of blocks, until it is high enough.
steps.warn: Keep your fingers out from under the load. Push blocks in with another block or your foot.

steps.text: To move it along the floor, set it on three round pipes and push. Move the pipe that comes out at the back round to the front.
For tall loads like fridges and washers, strap the load to a hand truck before tipping it back.
To load a vehicle, use a ramp of strong planks and a strap, or a jack or winch. Strap everything down before you drive.
Stop when you're tired. Most lifting injuries happen at the end of the day.

notes:
## Rules of thumb

- A fit adult can lift about 20–25 kg close to the body at waist height. Reaching, twisting, lifting from the floor or above the shoulder, and tiredness all cut that a lot.
- Two people can lift less than double what one can, because they can't both hold it ideally.
- If you need to strain, stop and get help or a tool.

## Common salvage weights

| Item | Rough weight |
|---|---|
| Microwave oven transformer | 6–9 kg |
| Car battery | 15–25 kg |
| Golf cart battery | about 30 kg |
| Treadmill | about 80 kg |
| Fridge or washing machine | 50 kg or more |
| Vending machine | several hundred kilograms |

## Levers

A lever multiplies your push by the ratio of the two arms. A 1 m bar with the pivot block 10 cm from the load gives about 9 times your push at the load. Lift a little, block it, reposition.

## Common mistakes

- Lifting with a rounded back.
- Gloves with no grip.
- Walking backwards down stairs with nobody guiding.
- Trying to catch a falling load.
- Carrying a load you can't see past.
